---

The official Ruby library for the Tungo Platform API (`https://api.tungo.kz`): the AI accountant, 1C integration, bank statements, e-invoices, tax forms and automations of [Tungo AI](https://tungo.kz).

It is generated from the API's OpenAPI contract, so its methods and models always match the contract it was built from.

## Requirements

Ruby 3.2 or newer; the test suite runs on Ruby 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 4.0. HTTP goes through `Net::HTTP` from the standard library with persistent connections. The only runtime dependencies are `base64` and `bigdecimal`, default gems that newer Rubies load only when they are declared. RBS signatures for the whole public API ship in `sig/`.

## Installation

```sh
bundle add tungo-sdk
# or
gem install tungo-sdk
```

Load it with `require "tungo"` (Bundler's automatic require works too; `require "tungo-sdk"` is an alias).

## Quick start

```ruby
require "tungo"

client = Tungo::Client.new(api_key: ENV.fetch("TUNGO_API_KEY"), company_id: "co_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q")

result = client.ask("Покажи дебиторку за октябрь")
puts result.answer
puts "dialog #{result.dialog_id}"

client.companies.list.data.each { |company| puts company.name }
```

## Authentication and configuration

Create one client and share it: it is immutable and safe to use from several threads or tasks. Every option can be passed explicitly; five of them fall back to environment variables.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `TUNGO_API_KEY` | none |
| Base URL | `TUNGO_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tungo.kz` |
| Webhook secret | `TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | none |
| Default company | `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID` | none |
| Default workspace | `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID` | none |
| Timeout | | 60 s (600 s for non-streaming chat turns) |
| Maximum retries | | 2 |
| Default headers, HTTP client | | none, built-in |

The API key is sent only to operations that require it; public endpoints and incoming hooks never receive it, and it never appears in error messages or debug output. Calling an authenticated operation without a key fails locally, before any request is made.

Every method also accepts per-request options: timeout, maximum retries, extra headers, an idempotency key and cancellation.

```ruby
client = Tungo::Client.new(
  api_key: ENV.fetch("TUNGO_API_KEY"),       # default: ENV["TUNGO_API_KEY"]
  base_url: ENV.fetch("TUNGO_BASE_URL"),     # default: ENV["TUNGO_BASE_URL"], then the production API
  webhook_secret: "whsec_c2VjcmV0",          # default: ENV["TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]
  company_id: "co_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q",
  workspace_id: "ws_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q",
  timeout: 60,
  max_retries: 2,
  default_headers: { "X-App" => "billing" }
)

# Per-request options
dialog = client.chat.get(
  "0b5f6a0e-6a1c-4d55-9a57-2f1d8b9c3e10",
  request_options: { timeout: 10, max_retries: 0, extra_headers: { "X-Trace" => "abc" } }
)
puts dialog.api_response.request_id
puts dialog.api_response.rate_limit&.remaining
```

Parameters are keyword arguments: path ids are positional, everything else is named. `nil` and "not given" are different: `nil` is sent as JSON `null` where the API accepts it, an argument you leave out is not sent at all. Company-scoped methods use the client's `company_id` unless you pass `company_id:` to the call (the same goes for `workspace_id`); the two defaults also fall back to `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID` and `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID`.

Every result exposes the HTTP response it came from through `api_response` (status, headers, request id, rate-limit headers of that very response); operations without a response body return it directly. To cancel a call, interrupt its thread (`Thread#raise`, `Thread#kill`, `Timeout.timeout`): sockets and back-off sleeps are interruptible and the connection is closed.

The API key must be printable ASCII without spaces or line breaks: a key read from a file with its trailing newline is refused with `Tungo::ConfigError` when the client is built (the key itself is never printed). `default_headers:` that carry credentials (`Authorization`, `X-Api-Key`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`) are sent only to operations authenticated with the API key, never to `POST /hooks/{token}` or to public endpoints; a header given for one call through `request_options: { extra_headers: ... }` is always sent.

`client.close` closes the pooled connections. `Tungo::Client.new(transport: Tungo::Transport::NetHTTP.new(proxy: "http://proxy:8080") { |http| http.ca_file = "ca.pem" })` customises the connections; any object with the same `execute` method can replace the transport.

## Errors

Every failure is a subtype of the SDK's base error. An HTTP error response becomes an API error chosen by the `error.type` field of the response body, falling back to the HTTP status when the body is not the API's error envelope:

| `error.type` | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | 400 |
| `authentication_error` | 401 |
| `payment_required_error` | 402 |
| `permission_error` | 403 |
| `not_found_error` | 404 |
| `conflict_error` | 409 |
| `gone_error` | 410 |
| `limit_error` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500 |
| `unavailable_error` | 503 |

An API error carries the status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, the parsed retry-after delay, the response headers and the raw body. Problems that happen without a response have their own types: connection error, timeout, decode error (a successful response whose body is not valid), and configuration or validation error (raised before any request).

```ruby
begin
  client.proposals.approve("P-000042")
rescue Tungo::LimitError => e
  warn "Limit reached, retry in #{e.retry_after} s"
rescue Tungo::InvalidRequestError => e
  e.fields.each { |field| warn "#{field.path}: #{field.message}" }
rescue Tungo::APIError => e
  warn "#{e.status} #{e.type} #{e.code}: #{e.api_message} (request #{e.request_id})"
rescue Tungo::TimeoutError, Tungo::ConnectionError => e
  warn "Network problem: #{e.message}"
end
```

The class names are `Tungo::InvalidRequestError`, `AuthenticationError`, `PaymentRequiredError`, `PermissionError`, `NotFoundError`, `ConflictError`, `GoneError`, `LimitError`, `ServerError` (`api_error`) and `UnavailableError`, all subclasses of `Tungo::APIError`. Without a response the SDK raises `Tungo::ConnectionError`, `Tungo::TimeoutError`, `Tungo::DecodeError`, `Tungo::ConfigError` or `Tungo::ValidationError`; all of them inherit from `Tungo::Error`, and the original exception is kept in `cause`.

`Tungo::DecodeError` means the API answered with a success status but the body could not be used: it is not JSON, it is empty, a declared property has the wrong JSON kind (a string where the contract says number, an object where it says array, and so on), a stream call was answered with something other than `text/event-stream`, or a chat stream ended before its `done` event. The check of kinds is deliberately light: only the properties of the top-level object, and `null`, missing properties, unknown properties and unknown enumeration values are always accepted. The error carries `api_response` and the raw `body`. The request itself was accepted by the server, so do not repeat a write because of it.

`client.ask` raises the typed `Tungo::APIError` when the turn reports an error in its `errors` list; pass `raise_on_error: false` to get the result with the errors instead.

## Retries and timeouts

A request is retried up to 2 times (3 attempts) on connection errors, timeouts and the statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, but only when repeating it is safe: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests, and `POST` or `PATCH` requests of the operations whose contract declares an `Idempotency-Key`. For those the SDK generates a random key and reuses it for every attempt; you can pass your own. Other operations send no key, not even one you pass, because the API would ignore it.

The delay between attempts is `min(0.5 s × 2^attempt, 8 s)` with random jitter. A positive `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After` response header overrides it; if the server asks for more than 60 s the SDK does not wait and raises the error with the delay filled in.

The timeout covers the whole request including reading the body. Streaming calls have no total timeout, only a connect timeout and an idle timeout of 120 s. Cancellation supplied by the caller is combined with the timeout.

```ruby
client = Tungo::Client.new(max_retries: 5, timeout: 20)

client.companies.list(request_options: { max_retries: 0, timeout: 5 })
client.proposals.approve("P-000042", request_options: { idempotency_key: "approve-P-000042" })
```

`chat_timeout:` (600 s) is the client-wide timeout of non-streaming chat turns; `connect_timeout:` and `stream_idle_timeout:` apply to streams. A per-request `timeout:` overrides them for one call. The total timeout covers connecting, sending and reading the whole body. A `Retry-After` of zero, a negative one or a date in the past is treated as absent: the SDK waits its normal back-off instead of retrying at once.

## Pagination

List operations use cursor pagination (`{ data, next_cursor }`). The plain method returns one typed page that knows whether there is a next page and can fetch it. The auto-paging variant is a lazy iterator: it requests the next page only when needed, carries your filters over, and stops fetching as soon as you stop iterating.

```ruby
page = client.proposals.list(status: "previewed", limit: 50)
page.data.each { |proposal| puts proposal.title }
page = page.next_page if page.next_page?

client.proposals.list_all(status: "previewed").each do |proposal|
  puts "#{proposal.id} #{proposal.total.formatted}"
end

first_ten = client.proposals.list_all.first(10)
puts first_ten.size
```

`*_all` returns a plain `Enumerator`, so `first`, `take_while`, `lazy` and friends work and fetch only the pages they need. If the API ever returns a cursor it has already returned during the walk (not only the previous one), a `Tungo::PaginationError` is raised instead of looping forever.

## Streaming

Streaming operations use server-sent events and deliver typed events as they arrive. Leaving the loop early or closing the stream closes the connection. A stream request is retried only before its first byte; an error response is raised as the same typed API error as for ordinary calls. A chat stream that ends before its final event is reported as an error, never as a finished answer.

```ruby
stream = client.chat.create_stream(message: "Сколько НДС к уплате за III квартал?")
turn = stream.each_text { |delta| print delta }
puts
puts "dialog #{turn.dialog_id}, turn #{turn.turn_no}, stop reason #{turn.stop_reason}"

# Or handle every typed event yourself; leaving the block closes the connection.
client.chat.create_stream(message: "Привет").each do |event|
  case event
  when Tungo::Models::ChatEventText then print event.delta
  when Tungo::Models::ChatEventTool then puts "[#{event.name}]"
  when Tungo::Models::ChatEventDone then break
  end
end
```

All five streaming operations work the same way: `chat.create_stream`, `chat.answer_stream`, `chat.list_events`, `batches.list_events` (typed `ChatEvent` variants, as a `Tungo::ChatStream`) and `feed.list_events` (`FeedItem` objects). Heart-beats are skipped; `each_sse` yields the raw events instead. `accumulate` and `each_text` raise the typed `Tungo::APIError` if the turn reports an error, and `Tungo::DecodeError` ("stream ended before completion") if the stream ends with neither a `done` nor an `error` event, so a cut answer never looks like a finished turn; plain `each` simply ends. A success answer whose `Content-Type` is not `text/event-stream` raises `Tungo::DecodeError` when the stream is opened. The exception is a finished chat turn that the API replays for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (`application/json` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`): its stored result arrives as the events of that turn, ending with `done`. A stream can be consumed once; it may be handed to another thread and read or closed there (each request runs on a worker thread of the transport), but not read by two threads at once. Pass `last_event_id:` to resume the pure event streams.

## Webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are signed according to the Standard Webhooks specification (Svix). The verify helper takes the raw request body and the headers (`webhook-*` or `svix-*`), checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and the timestamp within 300 s of the system clock, and returns the typed event. Any problem is reported as a webhook verification error. If no secret is passed, the client's webhook secret is used.

The send-hook helper posts an event to an incoming hook (`/hooks/{token}`) and, when given a secret, signs the exact bytes it sends in the `X-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header. The API key is never sent to hooks.

```ruby
# In a Rack or Rails endpoint: pass the raw body and the request headers.
event = client.verify_webhook(request.body.read, request.env)
case event
when Tungo::Models::WebhookEventProposalWritten
  puts "Proposal #{event.data.proposal_id} was written"
else
  puts "Unhandled event #{event.type}"
end

# Send an event to an incoming hook, signed with the hook's secret.
accepted = client.send_hook("th_AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA",
                            { id: "order_1532", amount_tiyn: 4_500_000 }, secret: "hksec_secret")
puts accepted.event_id
```

`Tungo::Webhooks.verify_webhook(payload, headers, secret)` does the same without a client. Headers can be a Hash, a Rack env or any header collection. `Tungo::Webhooks.verify_hook_signature(body, signature, secret)` checks the `X-Signature` of an incoming hook on your side.

## Money

The API expresses amounts in tiyn (1/100 of a tenge) as 64-bit integers. The money helper converts decimal strings and exact decimal values to tiyn without floating-point error, rounding half away from zero (`"1.005"` → `101`), and formats tiyn for display (`4500000` → `45 000,00 ₸`). Invalid input raises a typed error.

```ruby
Tungo::Money.to_tiyn("1.005") # => 101
Tungo::Money.to_tiyn(BigDecimal("45000.5")) # => 4_500_050
Tungo::Money.format_tiyn(4_500_000) # => "45 000,00 ₸"
Tungo::Money.format_tiyn(-50, "USD") # => "-0,50 $"
Tungo::Money.to_tenge(4_500_050) # => BigDecimal("45000.5")
Tungo::Money.valid_bin_iin?("990140000017") # => true
```

Numbers with a fraction in API responses (such as `Money#amount`) are parsed as `BigDecimal`, never as `Float`, and a `BigDecimal` you pass in is sent digit for digit. `to_tiyn` also accepts `Integer`, `Rational` and, for convenience, `Float` (converted through its shortest decimal representation). Invalid input raises `Tungo::MoneyError`.

## Models

Every schema of the contract is a class under `Tungo::Models`: an immutable value object with typed readers.

```ruby
company = client.companies.get
company.name                # typed reader
company[:some_new_field]    # a field this SDK version does not know yet
company.key?(:bin)          # present (even when null) or absent?
company.to_h                # plain Ruby data with symbol keys
company.to_json             # exactly what travels on the wire
```

Enumerations are modules with one constant per known value (`Tungo::Models::ProposalStatus::PREVIEWED`); the readers return plain strings, so a value added by a newer API passes through. Unions with a discriminator (`ChatEvent`, `WebhookEvent`, ...) decode to the matching variant class and to `Tungo::UnknownVariant` for a variant this version does not know.

## Long-running helpers

```ruby
run = client.run_scenario_and_wait("scn_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q", timeout: 300)
puts run.state

job = client.upload_bank_statement(Pathname("kl_to_1c.txt"))
job = client.wait_for_batch(job.id)
puts job.running
```

The wait helpers poll with a pause that grows from 1 s to 5 s and raise `Tungo::WaitTimeoutError` (a `Tungo::TimeoutError`) when the deadline (`timeout:`, 600 s by default) passes. `send_hook` and `automations.post_hook` send the `event_id` you pass as the `Idempotency-Key`, and a random UUID when you pass none.

## Versioning and support

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While the major version is 0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; they are always listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-ruby/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). This README describes version 0.3.0.

The code is generated: please report problems and ideas in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-ruby/issues) rather than opening pull requests against generated files. To report a vulnerability, follow the [security policy](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-ruby/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
